newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees refining capacity up in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees refining capacity up in 1997/98.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Wednesday that its total refining capacity would increase to 1.10 million barrels per day (bpd) in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from an estimated 999,500 bpd at the end of 1996/97.
Pertamina now has eight refineries with a combined capacity of 989,500 bpd and the small Kasim refinery in Irian Jaya will add capacity of 1,000 bpd from February.

"We project total refining capacity will rise to 1.10 million barrels per day in fiscal 1997/98. The projection is mostly based on additional capacity from the debottlenecking of Cilacap refinery and the small new refinery in Irian Jaya," M.S.M Situmorang, head of Pertamina's technical processing division, told reporters.
He said the debottlenecking of Cilacap refinery, in Central Java, was expected to be completed in 1998 and would add 48,000 bpd to its 300,000 bpd capacity.
He said Pertamina also will add 25,000 bpd capacity to its 252,000 bpd Balikpapan refinery, in East Kalimantan, in 1998.
Other planned increases include a capacity increase of 30,000 bpd in the Dumai refinery in Sumatra, Situmorang said without giving any details.
